# tests/fixtures/contract/

Recorded (request, response) pairs for the Bhashini `/health`, `/asr`,
`/nmt`, and `/tts` endpoints, one JSON file per call, generated by:

```
python -m services.mock_bhashini --port 18400 &
python -m tools.capture_bhashini_contract --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18400 --record --out-dir tests/fixtures/contract
```

These were captured against `services.mock_bhashini` (the dev-only fake),
**not** the real device -- we don't have the Jetson until 5 Aug 2026. They
exist so `tests/_fake_http.py`'s `FakeSession.from_fixture_dir()` can
replay real (request, response) shapes in hermetic client tests without
starting any server.

On 6 Aug, re-run the capture command above with `--base-url` pointing at
the real device to get a *real* corpus, then run
`tools/verify_contract.py` to see exactly where the real device's
responses differ from what's recorded here -- most importantly, whether
the language-code casing this repo assumed
(`puriyudha/clients/bhashini.py`'s `_LANGUAGE_CODES` table) actually
matches what the real service expects.
